title: Hydrogel-Based Flexible Sensors: From Manufacturing Strategies to Sensing Applications

abstract.original: Abstract Hydrogel-based flexible sensors combine tissue-like mechanical properties with superior sensing performance, showing immense potential in human-machine interaction, soft robotics, and health monitoring. Although significant progress has been made in related research, the fabrication of precision structures, the environmental tolerance of materials, and the heterogeneous integration between materials and devices remain key research challenges. In response to these challenges, this review provides a comprehensive review of the latest progress in hydrogel-based sensors, covering the entire process from material fabrication and functional regulation to interface engineering. First, the impacts of advanced processing techniques such as solution processing, microstructure molding, photolithography, additive manufacturing, and fiber spinning on film structure are discussed in detail. Subsequently, physicochemical strategies for enhancing sensing performance and environmental tolerance are analyzed. Furthermore, diverse assembly schemes and interface engineering strategies are highlighted. Finally, typical applications in pressure, strain, environmental, and physiological signal monitoring are summarized. This review aims to provide guidance for the development of next-generation high-performance and stable flexible electronic systems.

by next-generation sensors. Second, synergistically optimising synthetic strategies and encapsulation
techniques to confer structural integrity and functional stability across diverse environments remains an urgent
manufacturing challenge[52]. Moreover, the fabrication of flexible sensors inherently involves a cross-scale
heterogeneous integration process. The unique ‘soft and wet’ properties of hydrogels result in significant
mechanical mismatches with rigid electrodes and encapsulation layers[53, 54]. The establishment of robust
heterogeneous interfaces during manufacturing to prevent delamination and failure under dynamic loads
represents a major technical bottleneck in current device processing.
This review comprehensively explores the latest research advances in hydrogel-based flexible sensors
and systematically investigates hydrogel synthesis techniques, functional tuning strategies, sensor assembly
processes, application domains, as well as current challenges and future development trends (see Figure 2).
The structure of this paper is as follows: section 2 provides a comprehensive overview of advanced
manufacturing techniques for hydrogels, encompassing solution processing, microstructure molding,
photolithography, additive manufacturing, and fiber spinning, which serve as the cornerstone for achieving
customised device structures. Section 3 introduces performance-tuning strategies for hydrogels, systematically
examining approaches to constructing conductive networks, designing for extreme environmental adaptability,
implementing self-healing mechanisms, achieving biocompatibility, and imparting antimicrobial properties.
Section 4 summarizes structural design principles for hydrogel-based sensors, focusing on heterogeneous
interface connection strategies and device encapsulation solutions. Section 5 outlines the applications of
hydrogel-based sensors in monitoring pressure, strain, environment, and bioelectrical signals, demonstrating
their immense potential in flexible electronics and intelligent systems. Finally, Section 6 analyses unresolved
key issues and technical bottlenecks in current hydrogel-based sensor research while outlining future
development directions. This review aims to provide systematic theoretical underpinnings for the preparation
of high-performance hydrogels and the design and fabrication of sensors. Concurrently, it is hoped that this
